headline: Rhode Island Route 10-to-I-95 ramp closes Friday night for interchange work
dek: RIDOT will shut the Route 10 South ramp to I-95 North from 9 p.m. Friday until before Monday’s morning commute, then shift the ramp entrance as the Providence-Cranston interchange rebuild continues.
body: Drivers heading from Route 10 South to Interstate 95 North at the Providence-Cranston line should expect a weekend detour beginning Friday night. The Rhode Island Department of Transportation says the ramp will close at 9 p.m. on Oct. 2 and reopen before the morning commute on Monday, Oct. 5, while crews connect a newly built bridge to the roadway leading toward I-95 North. The schedule remains subject to weather and construction conditions, according to RIDOT’s [I-95 15 project update](https://www.dot.ri.gov/projects/The-I-95-15/).

RIDOT’s signed detour sends drivers onto the ramp for I-95 South, then off at Exit 31C for Jefferson Boulevard. From there, motorists will turn left onto Jefferson Boulevard and left again to reach the northbound I-95 on-ramp. That route adds decisions and turning movements to a connection many commuters use to move between Cranston, Providence and the broader interstate network, so drivers who normally make the Route 10-to-I-95 North move will need to watch for temporary signs and allow extra time.

The closure is only one step in the traffic plan. On Friday, before the nighttime shutdown, RIDOT expects to shift the beginning of the Route 10 South-to-I-95 North ramp about 100 feet from its current position. Drivers will enter the ramp sooner after the shift, while the nearby on-ramp to I-95 South will not change. Once the northbound ramp reopens, motorists will be using the new alignment rather than returning to the present entrance.

More changes are planned for mid-October at the Route 1, or Elmwood Avenue, northbound ramp to Route 10 North. RIDOT says drivers will have to choose a lane based on where they are going after the merge: the right lane for I-95 North, or the left lane for Route 10 toward Providence and Exit 1C for I-95 South. The department plans additional signs and pavement markings, and says that arrangement will remain through spring 2027.

The Providence Journal reported Sept. 25 that the work is part of a larger effort to turn the Route 10 segment between Park Avenue and the I-95 interchange into a boulevard-style connection. The newspaper said the planned design is intended to create a direct link between Elmwood Avenue and Park Avenue, with a shared-use bike path and improved pedestrian connections to Roger Williams Park. That broader street design means the current ramp closures are tied to a long construction sequence, not a short resurfacing job.

The scale of the corridor helps explain why a weekend ramp closure can affect more than the immediate interchange. RIDOT says the I-95 15 project corridor between Providence and Warwick carries about 185,000 vehicles each day, including roughly 9,000 trucks and other heavy freight vehicles. The agency also identifies hospitals, businesses and universities along the route, making reliable access important for commuters, deliveries and regional trips even when the affected ramp is only one part of the highway system.

The project is designed to address 15 bridges rated poor or fair but nearing poor condition along I-95 and Route 10. RIDOT lists Providence, Cranston and Warwick as the project locations, a projected cost of $779 million and a construction schedule running from 2024 through 2031. The department says a $251 million federal Bridge Investment Program grant helps offset the cost. It also says the work will remove three of Rhode Island’s five most-traveled structurally deficient bridges from that list.

For Friday-night travelers, the immediate issue is the Route 10 South ramp closure and the signed Jefferson Boulevard detour. For regular commuters, the more lasting change will be learning the shifted entrance and the later lane assignments near Elmwood Avenue. RIDOT says construction schedules and traffic patterns can change with weather, project needs and field conditions, so drivers should check the department’s travel information and follow the signs in place when they approach the interchange.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Rhode Island Route 10 to I-95 ramp closure begins Oct. 2
seoDescription: RIDOT will close the Route 10 South ramp to I-95 North at the Providence-Cranston line from Friday night through early Monday for bridge work.
